items.briefing:
Cybercriminals are increasingly using AI to speed up attacks, and a recent case saw an entirely AI-driven ransomware attack unfold with minimal human involvement — a sign of how quickly threats are evolving. Separately, a serious security flaw has been found in SonicWall SMA 1000 devices that allows attackers to break in without needing a password; if your organisation uses these devices, urgent patching is needed. There are also reports of voice call ("vishing") scams targeting Microsoft Teams users, which is relevant given how widely Teams is used across Australian workplaces and training organisations.

**Practical tip:** If you receive an unexpected call or Teams message asking you to click a link or provide login details — even if it appears to be from IT support — hang up and verify directly with your IT team before doing anything.

featured.title: AI’s Vulnerability Surge May Be More Manageable Than First Feared
featured.summary: New research suggests the coming Vulnpocalypse may not be so overwhelming for enterprise security teams — if they have the right strategies.
